reviews.reasoning: Independent re-derivation. NUMBERING: Ps 89 is a shift+1 psalm; ps_lib.web_to_mt maps web:Ps.89.46-51 onto oshb:Ps.89.47-52 verse for verse, and 6 of 6 in-span pairings in boundary_evidence_refs are arithmetically correct (citation_sweep.py GREEN, 0 problems). The span is a WEB-contiguous block that abuts the doxology verse with 0 gaps and 0 overlaps. FRONT SEAM web:Ps.89.45|89.46 = oshb:Ps.89.46|89.47: the MT verse before the seam closes on סֶֽלָה (oshb:Ps.89.46 = web:Ps.89.45, collate byte tier; the pmarks_Ps.json selah inventory for Ps 89 is 4 verses — MT 89:5, 89:38, 89:46, 89:49 — at 1 occurrence apiece), and the MT verse after it opens עַד מָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.89.47 = web:Ps.89.46, collate byte tier), an interrogative opener rendered “How long, Yahweh?” at web:Ps.89.46. The seam therefore rests on a tier-1 discourse-mode shift, with selah as corroboration rather than as the driver, which is the correct weighting. SELAH SYMMETRY inside the span: selah falls in 1 of 6 verses of oshb:Ps.89.47-52, namely סֶֽלָה at oshb:Ps.89.49 = web:Ps.89.48 (byte tier), and the row discloses that occurrence explicitly, so the cross-seam-cohesion objection is pre-answered; check_marks.py GREEN. K/Q: pmarks_Ps.json records 2 ketiv/qere verses in Ps 89 (MT 89:18, 89:29), 0 of them inside oshb:Ps.89.47-52, so no K/Q disclosure was owed. Paseq sits at oshb:Ps.89.50 and oshb:Ps.89.52 (seg layer, single-witness); the row makes no paseq claim, and no such claim was owed. No pe/samekh claim appears, which is correct — pmarks_Ps.json carries an empty marks object for the whole book. BACK SEAM web:Ps.89.51|89.52 = oshb:Ps.89.52|89.53 is the doxology cut and is byte-clean. UNCITED CORROBORATION the row could have used: the consonantal root ז-כ-ר opens both זְכָר (oshb:Ps.89.48 = web:Ps.89.47) and זְכֹ֣ר (oshb:Ps.89.51 = web:Ps.89.50), bracketing the span's interior from inside — that is cohesion for the span, not against it. The 4 WEB spans quoted in the rationale beside a web: ref check out verbatim, 4 of 4 (check_web_quotes.py reports 0 verbatim failures); check_refs_mirror.py GREEN (the 1 out-of-span verse argued in prose, web:Ps.89.45, is carried in boundary_evidence_refs); check_language_zones.py GREEN. unit_type strophe and confidence medium are both defensible — the driver is a mode shift rather than a superscription or a doxology, so medium is calibrated. The span and the warrant survive. What does not survive is the evidence form: the rejected_alternative field breaches the mandatory curly-quote-plus-inline-web:-ref convention (machine-flagged), and the row quotes 0 pointed-Hebrew runs for a driver that is an original-language claim. Both are filed below.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative field carries 2 curly-quoted WEB spans that lack a web: ref in the same field, breaching the mandatory quote-plus-inline-ref convention and leaving both quotations machine-unverifiable (check_web_quotes.py exits 1 on this row).
challenges.evidence: check_web_quotes.py on this row exits 1 with 2 flags, 2 of 2 curly-quoted spans in that field, both at path [0].rejected_alternative, issue 'curly quote with NO web: ref in its field', for the spans 'How long, Yahweh?' and 'You have' plus ellipsis. That field carries exactly 1 reference, the bare '(89:46)', which lacks the web: prefix the checker binds on. TOOLKIT.md states the requirement without exception: 'CURLY QUOTES + an inline web: ref in the SAME field are MANDATORY at every layer' (1 of 1 fields here breaches it). This is a verifiability defect, not a falsity defect — I checked both spans against the bytes: “How long, Yahweh?” opens web:Ps.89.46 (= oshb:Ps.89.47) and “You have shortened the days of his youth.” opens web:Ps.89.45 (= oshb:Ps.89.46), so the quoted material and the verse number are both right; as delivered the checker cannot bind them. CURE: prefix the field's existing bare ref as web:Ps.89.46 (dual-citing to oshb:Ps.89.47 if the pairing is wanted in-field). The same 2 spans in the rationale field pass, because that field does carry web: refs — the defect is confined to rejected_alternative.

challenges.claim: The row holds 0 pointed-Hebrew runs in any field, so its 1 tier-1 driver — the interrogative opener that replaces the declarative accusation series — is argued from the WEB rendering and is not shown in the original language.
challenges.evidence: The row holds 0 pointed-Hebrew runs in any field, yet its 1 tier-1 driver is an original-language claim: observed_substrate_signals asserts that interrogative address replaces the declarative accusation series as the unit's opening mode, and that claim is argued from the WEB rendering alone. TOOLKIT.md standing rule: 'Quote the original language for every boundary-relevant original-language claim' (0 of 1 drivers in this row satisfies it). The claim is TRUE — I derived it from the bytes rather than assuming it — which is why this is filed low: the interrogative opener is עַד מָ֣ה at oshb:Ps.89.47 = web:Ps.89.46 (collate byte tier), while the 2 MT verses immediately before the seam open with second-person perfect forms bearing the -ta suffix, הִ֭קְצַרְתָּ at oshb:Ps.89.46 = web:Ps.89.45 and הִשְׁבַּ֥תָּ at oshb:Ps.89.45 = web:Ps.89.44 (both byte tier), matching the WEB renderings “You have shortened the days of his youth.” at web:Ps.89.45 and “You have ended his splendor” at web:Ps.89.44. Those form labels are argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, since verse_map_oshb.json stages text, language and web fields, with 0 morphology fields. CURE: splice the interrogative opener into the rationale beside its existing dual-cited web:Ps.89.46 = oshb:Ps.89.47 pairing; 1 edit, and the WEB gloss stays as cut.

reviews.reasoning: Independent re-derivation. The Hebrew run quoted in the rationale collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Ps.89.53 and hits no other verse of the psalm (collate_hebrew run over 53 MT verses of Ps 89 returns 1 non-none result, tier byte, at Ps.89.53). The dual-cite web:Ps.89.52 = oshb:Ps.89.53 is correct for this shift+1 psalm and is carried both in-field beside the Hebrew (the preferred form) and in boundary_evidence_refs; the span uses the required X-X form for a 1-verse span; citation_sweep.py GREEN. The WEB quotation “Blessed be Yahweh forever more. Amen, and Amen” checks out verbatim against web:Ps.89.52, 1 of 1 spans checked. The internal anatomy of the claim is byte-true: the verse holds 5 tokens — baruch / YHWH / le-olam / amen / we-amen — so 'baruch followed by amen x2' is exactly what the bytes carry, and psalm_device_inventory.json book_boundary_doxologies independently records Ps.89.53 with baruch true and amen 2. unit_type coda and the Book III attribution (Psalms 73-89) are both correct against the five-book division. The boundary is the highest-tier macro class in the book (4 book-wide) and the high confidence is warranted — I contest neither the span, nor the unit_type, nor the confidence. What fails is the class parallel the warrant leans on: the row names Books I, II and V as the sites of the same closing class, and Book V (MT Ps 107-150) contains 0 verses of that class. The correct fourth site is Book IV at oshb:Ps.106.48, and even that site differs in amen count. The same wrong attribution is installed in observed_substrate_signals, a dependent field, so the cure is 1 edit written onto 2 fields. Filed below.

challenges.claim: The warrant's class parallel is factually wrong in 2 fields: the baruch-plus-amen closing class sits at the ends of Books I, II and IV, while Book V carries 0 verses with the amen token across MT Ps 107-150 (sweep unit: verses).
challenges.evidence: SWEEP (unit = MT verses). The standalone amen token was spliced from oshb:Ps.89.53's own bytes (token 4 of 5: אָ֘מֵ֥ן, collate byte tier against oshb:Ps.89.53) and swept book-wide as an exact accent-stripped TOKEN comparison, not as a skeleton substring: 4 verses. The skeleton-substring figure would be 5 verses and is the wrong object, because it drags in oshb:Ps.89.38, whose closing token is the adjective 'faithful'. The 4 exact-token verses are oshb:Ps.41.14 (= web:Ps.41.13), oshb:Ps.72.19 (= web:Ps.72.19), oshb:Ps.89.53 (= web:Ps.89.52) and oshb:Ps.106.48 (= web:Ps.106.48). Verses in MT Ps 107-150 (Book V) carrying that token: 0. Verses in Book V carrying the baruch token AND the amen token: 0. Those 4 verses sit at the ends of Books I (1-41), II (42-72), III (73-89) and IV (90-106) per the five-book division in psalm_device_inventory.json — the class is I, II, III (this row) and IV, so the row's 'V' names a site that does not exist. BYTES. Book IV's site: בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֪י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל מִן הָ֤עוֹלָ֨ם וְעַ֬ד הָעוֹלָ֗ם וְאָמַ֖ר כָּל הָעָ֥ם אָמֵ֗ן הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ (oshb:Ps.106.48 = web:Ps.106.48, collate byte tier), rendered “Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting!” at web:Ps.106.48. Book V's closing verse: כֹּ֣ל הַ֭נְּשָׁמָה תְּהַלֵּ֥ל יָ֗הּ הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ (oshb:Ps.150.6 = web:Ps.150.6, collate byte tier), rendered “Let everything that has breath praise Yah! Praise Yah!” at web:Ps.150.6 — it carries neither token. SECOND-ORDER. The row defines its class as baruch plus amen x2, and by amen token count per verse that stricter class runs oshb:Ps.41.14 = 2, oshb:Ps.72.19 = 2, oshb:Ps.89.53 = 2, oshb:Ps.106.48 = 1 (plus hallelu-Yah); under the row's own definition the parallels reduce to Books I and II (2 sites), with Book IV a near neighbour that differs in amen count. psalm_device_inventory.json records the same figures (Ps.41.14 amen 2, Ps.72.19 amen 2, Ps.89.53 amen 2, Ps.106.48 amen 1). CURE (1 edit, 2 fields): replace 'Books I, II, and V' in the rationale and 'the book I, II, and V closing doxologies' in observed_substrate_signals with the Book I, II and IV sites, disclosing that Book IV's site closes with 1 amen token plus hallelu-Yah.
